Section 1: The Premise of the Company

JD.com, Inc. operates as China's premier direct-sales (1P) e-commerce giant and supply chain technology platform. Unlike asset-light marketplace models, JD operates a vertically integrated operational engine backed by over 1,600 self-managed fulfillment warehouses and an in-house logistics network (JD Logistics). This heavy infrastructure enables fast same-day and next-day delivery ("211 delivery"), driving consumer trust in product authenticity, superior customer service, and reliable fulfillment across electronics, home appliances, general merchandise, and fresh grocery categories. The core economic engine operates on negative cash conversion cycles—collecting immediate digital payment from millions of retail shoppers while settling supplier payables on extended terms.

The business possesses a durable structural moat anchored by unmatched scale economics, low-cost logistics routing, and direct brand sourcing relationships that generate genuine pricing power. To evaluate the operational performance of this commercial engine, management and private enterprise owners monitor five primary operational metrics:

  • Annual Active Customers: Exceeded 700 million active shopping accounts.
  • Customer Shopping Frequency: Expanded at a >40% year-over-year growth rate.
  • JD Retail Operating Margin: Reached 4.6% for FY 2025 and 5.6% in Q1 2026, demonstrating expanding core profitability.
  • Fulfillment Expense Ratio: Maintained at 6.7% of total net revenues through automated warehouse routing.
  • Net Revenue Scale: Generated $187.20 billion USD in annual sales during FY 2025, solidifying its position as China's largest retailer by revenue.

To establish the true owner earnings generation of the enterprise without financial district distortion, we extract figures directly from audited SEC filings (Form 20-F and Form 6-K). In FY 2025, JD generated $6.11 billion USD (RMB 43.7 billion) in GAAP Operating Cash Flow. To isolate pure operating performance, $1.25 billion USD of non-operating interest income earned on massive cash holdings is deducted to prevent double-counting when valuing liquid assets on the balance sheet bridge. Deducting $2.80 billion USD in maintenance capital expenditures (out of $6.91 billion total CapEx that includes property developments and fulfillment center builds) and treating $0.59 billion USD (RMB 4.2 billion) of Stock-Based Compensation strictly as a 100% cash charge yields a conservative Core Baseline Owner Earnings (OE₀) of $1.47 billion USD.

The financial foundation is reinforced by a fortress balance sheet holding $32.20 billion USD (RMB 225.4 billion) in gross cash, restricted cash, and short-term investments. Deducting total funded debt and capital leases of $8.67 billion USD, reserving a calibrated 3.0% operational working capital buffer ($5.55 billion USD) to support $187.20B in retail volume, and accounting for $1.80 billion USD in committed cash outlays for the European acquisition of Ceconomy AG yields $16.48 billion USD in true unencumbered surplus cash. Distributed across 1.40 billion American Depositary Shares (ADSs, where 1 ADS = 2 Ordinary Shares), JD carries +$11.77 USD per ADS in liquid surplus backing. Applying Warren Buffett's country-adjusted opportunity cost hurdle rate of 9.5%–10.5% provides a rational hurdle for China enterprise valuation.

Executive Leadership Commentary & 4-Quarter Trajectory

Ms. Sandy Xu (Xu Ran), Chief Executive Officer: "Our user base and shopping frequency continued to expand robustly, with annual active customers hitting a new record—a clear testament to the deepening synergies across our business ecosystem. Core retail priorities have shifted from purely chasing top-line volume toward balancing revenue recovery with structural margin expansion, driving supply-chain efficiency and leveraging AI capabilities to narrow new business investments while reinforcing our 1P retail moat."

Mr. Ian Su Shan (Shan Su), Chief Financial Officer: "This financial performance was anchored by the steady progress of JD Retail, as general merchandise categories and high-frequency consumer goods gained strong momentum. With a fortress balance sheet featuring over $32 billion USD in liquid assets, we maintained rigorous capital allocation discipline—executing $3.0 billion USD in share repurchases during 2025 and paying $1.4 billion USD in annual cash dividends ($1.00 per ADS), returning substantial capital directly to enterprise owners."

Corporate Governance, VIE Structure & Capital Allocation Controls

Contractual VIE Architecture: Offshore investors hold equity in JD.com, Inc., a Cayman Islands exempted holding company. Operating assets in mainland China subject to foreign investment restrictions (value-added telecommunications, internet platforms, and logistics networks) are held via Variable Interest Entities (VIEs) governed through contractual arrangements. While VIEs contributed 6.8% of total 2025 revenues, offshore equity holders lack direct equity ownership in mainland operating licenses.

Dual-Class Voting Concentration: Governance power is tightly concentrated. Founder and Chairman Richard Qiangdong Liu holds high-vote Class B ordinary shares carrying 20 votes per share (compared to 1 vote per Class A share), exercising ~73.1% of total voting control. Minority shareholders rely entirely on founder capital allocation choices.

Onshore Cash Repatriation & Capital Restrictions: Approximately RMB 78.2 billion ($10.9 billion USD) of net assets residing in PRC subsidiaries and VIEs remain subject to statutory reserve rules and state foreign exchange controls. Repatriating mainland cash to fund offshore ADS share buybacks or dividend distributions requires formal regulatory approval and incurs a 5% to 10% dividend withholding tax under PRC tax laws.

JD.com stands at a pivotal operational inflection point. After an intense period of capital spending on immediate-delivery initiatives (JD Food Delivery and 7Fresh Kitchen) that temporarily compressed overall operating margins, management has instituted strict capital discipline—cutting new business operating losses by over 50%. Concurrently, JD is expanding its supply chain beyond domestic borders through the €2.2 billion EUR takeover of Ceconomy AG (parent company of MediaMarkt and Saturn), securing controlling ownership across 1,000+ European consumer electronics stores. By combining disciplined cash generation in core retail, aggressive share repurchases, and strategic European expansion, JD is pivoting from market share defense back to durable owner value creation.

Section 2: 3 Probable Business Stories

Based on the company's core premise, reported operational metrics, financial filings, and 4-quarter earnings trajectory, here are 3 distinct, probable fundamental paths that cover 90%–95% of probable business outcomes over the next 3–5 years:

📖 Story 1: High-Margin 3P Expansion, European Infrastructure Scaling & Supply Chain Synergy

In this primary operational expansion trajectory, JD successfully executes a dual transformation: expanding high-margin third-party (3P) merchant monetization in domestic retail while completing and integrating the €2.2 billion ($1.80 billion cash outlay) takeover of Europe's largest electronics retailer, Ceconomy AG (parent of MediaMarkt and Saturn). Domestically, JD leverages its 1P fulfillment reputation to attract premium 3P merchants, expanding high-margin marketplace commission and advertising revenues. Internationally, JD digitizes Ceconomy’s 1,000+ European storefronts using its automated warehouse technology and logistics routing, transforming an offline retail chain into a high-efficiency omnichannel engine. Concurrently, management maintains strict loss-containment discipline across new initiatives (JD Food Delivery and 7Fresh), narrowing new business drag by over 50%.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Annual active customer accounts grow from 700 million toward 830 million, supported by double-digit growth in Plus subscriptions and grocery shopping frequency. Domestic 1P retail revenue grows at a steady 3.5% to 4.5% annual rate, while 3P marketplace/advertising services revenue accelerates at 8.0% to 11.0% annually. The full consolidation of Ceconomy AG (adding ~$24.0 billion USD in annual European retail sales) expands group top-line net revenues from the baseline of $187.20 billion USD in FY 2025 to $242.00 billion USD by Year 5 (a 5-year revenue CAGR of ~5.3%).

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Group gross margin expands from 16.5% to 18.2% driven by higher-margin service revenues and scale benefits in procurement. The fulfillment expense ratio drops from 6.7% to 6.1% as AI automated routing optimizes last-mile delivery. JD Retail operating margins widen from 4.6% baseline toward 5.8%. Total CapEx averages $4.50 billion USD annually ($3.10 billion USD maintenance CapEx for logistics maintenance and European store refits, and $1.40 billion USD growth CapEx for global fulfillment hubs). Deducting $3.10 billion USD maintenance CapEx, $0.65 billion USD in SBC, and interest adjustments from expanding operating cash flows pushes Core Baseline Owner Earnings from $1.47 billion USD (FY 2025) to $3.85 billion USD by Year 5.

Key Milestones to Watch: EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation regulatory clearance for Ceconomy AG; quarterly growth rate of 3P marketplace and marketing revenues (exceeding 8% YoY); and sustained JD Retail operating margin expansion above 5.0%.

📖 Story 2: Severe Price War Deflation, Negative Working Capital Unwind & European Integration Friction

This rigorous downside stress test models an environment of prolonged macroeconomic sluggishness in mainland China, aggressive structural price wars from competitors (Alibaba, PDD Holdings, and short-video e-commerce channels), and operational friction in Europe. Competitors aggressively subsidize core consumer electronics and home appliance categories, eroding JD’s historical pricing power and forcing defensive price cuts. Concurrently, strict European regulatory conditions (e.g., EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation constraints and localized labor union agreements) prevent JD from extracting planned supply-chain synergies from Ceconomy AG, turning the European acquisition into a low-margin capital drain.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Annual active customer accounts stall at ~690 million as price-sensitive consumers migrate to low-cost marketplace competitors. Shopping frequency on core high-ticket categories contracts, driving an 8.0% to 12.0% annual decline in electronics and home appliances revenue. Consolidated net revenues contract from the baseline of $187.20 billion USD down to $162.00 billion USD by Year 5 (a revenue CAGR of -2.8%).

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Gross margins compress from 16.5% to 14.2% as direct retail (1P) markup falls. JD Retail operating margins collapse from 4.6% to 2.1%. Crucially, as a direct-sales 1P retailer operating with large supplier trade payables, top-line contraction triggers a severe negative working capital unwind: JD must settle billions in legacy supplier liabilities without receiving sufficient cash inflows from new inventory sales, creating a cumulative $3.20 billion USD working capital cash drain over 3 years. GAAP Operating Cash Flow falls to $3.20 billion USD. Maintenance CapEx remains sticky at $2.60 billion USD to maintain warehouse networks, while SBC remains at $0.55 billion USD. Core Baseline Owner Earnings collapse from $1.47 billion USD down to $0.52 billion USD by Year 5 (a negative cash flow CAGR of -18.7%).

Key Milestones to Watch: YoY revenue contraction in electronics and home appliances exceeding -10%; gross margin compression below 15.0%; net cash outflows from working capital payables liquidation; and regulatory restrictions on European operational integration.

📖 Story 3: Domestic Cash-Cow Maturity, Strategic Capital Return & Warehouse Automation Efficiency

In this mature steady-state trajectory, JD accepts that Chinese direct-sales e-commerce has reached structural saturation. Management eschews unprofitable top-line market share battles and refrains from aggressive overseas land-grabs, opting to run Ceconomy AG strictly as a standalone, self-funded European subsidiary. Strategic focus shifts entirely toward maximizing cash flow per share from the core domestic retail engine through aggressive warehouse automation, supply chain AI optimization, and disciplined capital allocation—returning surplus cash directly to owners via share buybacks and steady annual dividends.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Active accounts remain highly stable at 720 million to 740 million, with growth concentrated in high-frequency general merchandise and supermarket items (+5.0% to 7.0% annually) offsetting mild softness in high-ticket electronics. Domestic retail revenues grow at a modest, inflation-like rate of 2.0% to 3.0% per year. Consolidated net revenues expand from $187.20 billion USD in FY 2025 to $212.00 billion USD by Year 5 (a 5-year revenue CAGR of ~2.5%).

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Group gross margin stabilizes at 17.0% to 17.5%. The fulfillment expense ratio improves steadily from 6.7% to 6.2% due to automated warehouse robotics and route density optimizations. Group operating margin stabilizes between 4.2% and 4.6%. Total CapEx is strictly restricted to maintenance levels averaging $2.70 billion USD annually, with zero discretionary growth CapEx. Stock-based compensation is capped at $0.50 billion USD per year. Core Baseline Owner Earnings expand predictably from $1.47 billion USD to $2.45 billion USD by Year 5 (an Owner Earnings CAGR of ~10.7%). Management allocates the $16.48 billion USD surplus net cash balance and recurring owner cash flows to repurchase 3.0% to 4.0% of outstanding ADSs annually while maintaining a $1.00 USD per ADS dividend.

Key Milestones to Watch: Fulfillment expense ratio reduction toward 6.0%; annual ADS repurchase volume exceeding $2.0 billion USD; discipline in maintaining growth CapEx near zero; and steady dividend payout continuity.

Step-by-Step Mathematical Proofs Across the 3 Paths

High-Margin 3P Expansion, European Infrastructure Scaling & Supply Chain Synergy ($42.69): JD expands high-margin 3P marketplace monetization while integrating European retailer Ceconomy AG into its supply chain network. Automated warehouse routing and loss containment across new business initiatives reduce fulfillment costs, pushing Year 5 Core Owner Earnings to $3.85B USD. Starting from baseline Owner Earnings of $1,470.0M compounding at +21.2% annually over 5 years (reaching $3,844.4M in Year 5), the discounted cash flows total $10,069.8M at a 9.5% discount rate. Capitalizing Year 5 terminal cash flow at 2.00% terminal growth produces a terminal value of $52,284.1M (PV $33,212.3M). Operating enterprise value equals $43,282.1M, or $30.92 per ADS across 1,400.0M diluted ADSs. Adding unencumbered balance sheet surplus net cash of +$11.77 per ADS yields an exact intrinsic fair value of $30.92 + $11.77 = $42.69 per ADS.

Severe Price War Deflation, Negative Working Capital Unwind & European Integration Friction ($16.62): Intense e-commerce competition and macro headwinds erode direct-sales gross margins and trigger a $3.2B negative working capital cash drain from declining supplier payables. Ceconomy faces European regulatory friction, compressing Year 5 Core Owner Earnings to $0.52B USD. Starting from baseline Owner Earnings of $1,470.0M contracting at -18.7% annually over 5 years (declining to $522.1M in Year 5), the discounted cash flows total $3,210.4M at a 10.5% discount rate. Capitalizing Year 5 terminal cash flow at 1.50% terminal growth produces a terminal value of $5,888.4M (PV $3,574.2M). Operating enterprise value contracts to $6,784.7M, or $4.85 per ADS across 1,400.0M diluted ADSs. Adding unencumbered balance sheet surplus net cash of +$11.77 per ADS yields an exact intrinsic fair value of $4.85 + $11.77 = $16.62 per ADS.

Domestic Cash-Cow Maturity, Strategic Capital Return & Warehouse Automation Efficiency ($32.27): JD runs core 1P retail as a mature cash cow, restricting discretionary growth CapEx while optimizing logistics efficiency via warehouse automation. Robust free cash flow generation and aggressive share repurchases support expansion of Year 5 Core Owner Earnings to $2.45B USD. Starting from baseline Owner Earnings of $1,470.0M compounding at +10.7% annually over 5 years (reaching $2,443.7M in Year 5), the discounted cash flows total $7,595.2M at a 9.5% discount rate. Capitalizing Year 5 terminal cash flow at 2.00% terminal growth produces a terminal value of $33,234.9M (PV $21,111.7M). Operating enterprise value equals $28,706.9M, or $20.50 per ADS across 1,400.0M diluted ADSs. Adding unencumbered balance sheet surplus net cash of +$11.77 per ADS yields an exact intrinsic fair value of $20.50 + $11.77 = $32.27 per ADS.
